structure.overview: The case concerns Westcoast Energy Inc. (applicant) appealing the Tax Court's decision rejecting its claim for input tax credits on reimbursed employee health services. The Tax Court held that the appellant did not acquire or receive the services under the relevant provisions of the Excise Tax Act, relying on the Supreme Court's prior decision in ExxonMobil Canada Ltd. The Federal Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, finding no legal or factual error in the Tax Court's decision and applying the precedent from ExxonMobil.

party_points.text: subsection 175(1) and subparagraph 170(1)(b)(ii) allow input tax credits for employee services
new oral argument on 'use' in section 173

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The appellant reimbursed employees for certain health services and claimed input tax credits, which the Minister rejected, leading to an appeal to the Tax Court.

citations.cite: Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15
citations.why: Statute governing goods and services tax and input tax credits

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The Tax Court held the appellant did not acquire or receive the services under the Act and dismissed the appeal.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The appellant accepts the Tax Court's findings but argues subsection 175(1) and subparagraph 170(1)(b)(ii) allow claiming input tax credits for employee services.

citations.why: Appellant's legal basis for claiming input tax credits
Appellant's additional legal basis for input tax credits

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: This Court's prior decision in ExxonMobil Canada Ltd. governs the appellant's submissions and the appeal's outcome.

citations.cite: ExxonMobil Canada Ltd. v. The Queen, 2010 FCA 1, 397 N.R. 204
citations.why: Precedent controlling the legal issue in this appeal

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court must follow prior decisions unless manifestly wrong; the appellant does not claim ExxonMobil is manifestly wrong, so it applies here.
idea_list: appellant does not claim manifest error

citations.cite: Miller v. Canada (Attorney General), 2002 FCA 370, 220 D.L.R. (4th) 149

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: ExxonMobil held that services for exclusive personal use of employees bear no relation to employer activities and thus subsection 175(1) does not apply to such reimbursements.

citations.why: Legal principle about exclusive personal use services

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Tax Court correctly found ExxonMobil applies equally to section 175 due to similar wording and roles, supported by Supreme Court emphasis on textual interpretation.
idea_list: Tax Court applied ExxonMobil to section 175

citations.cite: Canada Trustco Mortgage Co. v. Canada, 2005 SCC 54, [2005] 2 S.C.R. 601
citations.why: Supports textual interpretation of tax provisions

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: ExxonMobil held section 170 applies only if employer acquires a benefit for exclusive employee enjoyment; since appellant did not acquire services, section 170 does not apply.

citations.why: Clarifies section 170 applies only if employer acquires benefit

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appellant does not challenge ExxonMobil's correctness on section 170, and the Tax Court's analysis is sound.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: No legal error is found in the Tax Court's reasons.
idea_list: no legal error in Tax Court reasons

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appellant does not challenge the Tax Court's factual findings by palpable and overriding error, which would be the only other recourse.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The Tax Court found services were for exclusive personal use, employees did not acquire them for employment use, so subsection 175(1) does not apply; no error found.
idea_list: Tax Court factual findings on service use

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appellant's new oral argument on 'use' in section 173 was not considered by the Tax Court and lacks factual support here.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appeal is dismissed with costs.
